launch.title: Plan three View-style architectures for a notification center (Notice, NoticeList, NoticeTray)
steps: write the three options and the pick with decide.mjs

assign.now: read view-readme.md: chainable View over one element, tag factories, capturing (function child fills the box), subclasses render() into their own div, no DOM after await
wrote the decision with Server/decide.mjs into page.jsonl: three architectures (A tray owns data, B list owns data and emits, C DOM events only), B recommended at 0.75

decision.chose: B — NoticeList owns the array and emits add/remove/read; NoticeTray is bell + badge + box listening to the list; Notice is one message calling list.remove(this)
decision.alternative: A (tray owns data, direct child calls) is simpler for one tray but ties Notice to the tray; C (bubbling CustomEvents) hides wiring in event names

log: decide.mjs trap: a then entry must be a drafted child decision id, not prose; I had typed prose, then only unions, so I stripped the prose from decide-drafts.json (the tool's own draft store) and reran recommend. Four follow-on decisions drafted with --depends-on and logged too.

assign.now: nothing built, nothing to smoke-test: page.jsonl + task.jsonl only

outcome: Three View-style architectures for Notice / NoticeList / NoticeTray, with pros and cons, written as one decision plus four follow-ons in page.jsonl (Decisions module placed). Pick: B, the list owns the data and emits; the tray only listens.
